question: What is the difference between a property assessment and a property tax bill in the Northwest Territories?
generated_answer:
Property assessment is the process of placing a dollar value on a property for taxation purposes. You will receive a notice of assessment, which shows the assessed value of your property. Your property tax bill is calculated by multiplying the assessed value by the tax rate that applies to your property.

The assessed value of your property is used to determine how much you will pay in property tax. If you disagree with the assessed value of your property, you can file an appeal with the Northwest Territories Assessment Appeal Board.

Property tax bills are issued annually, usually in July or August. The amount of property tax you pay is determined by the assessed value of your property and the tax rate that applies to your property. The tax rate is set by the Government of the Northwest Territories and is applied to the assessed value of your property to determine the amount of property tax you will pay.
